bib.title: AnyTool: Self-Reflective, Hierarchical Agents for Large-Scale API Calls

read.skipped: Figures 1-7 are charts or diagrams; values not extracted from text.

question: Can a GPT-4 function-calling agent with a hierarchical API retriever and self-reflection solve queries over 16K+ RapidAPI APIs without training any module?
hypothesis: A hierarchical divide-and-conquer retriever plus a closed-loop self-reflection mechanism outperforms trained retrievers and flat GPT-4 retrieval; a larger API pool gives more chance of a relevant API.
contributions: AnyTool: plug-and-play hierarchical API retriever (meta/category/tool agents), solver (DFSDT or CoT) and self-reflection loop on GPT-4 function calling
Revised evaluation protocol (Eq 2) that removes the 'non-solvable counts as solved' inflation of ToolLLM's Eq 1
AnyToolBench, 400 solvable queries over the whole API pool
Filtered ToolBench with non-solvable queries removed by manual review

method.summary: A meta-agent creates category agents, which create tool agents; tool agents add APIs to a global candidate pool via function calls until check_if_request_solvable returns True. A single GPT-4 solver (DFSDT or CoT) answers from the pool; if GPT-4 judges the answer unsolved or the solver gives up, agents are re-activated bottom-up with the failure reason, and the solver reruns on the expanded pool.
method.task: tool/API use over a 16K+ API pool (retrieve then solve)

datasets.name: Filtered ToolBench
datasets.source: ToolBench (Qin et al., 2023b), manually filtered by authors
datasets.preprocessing: Removed non-solvable queries: missing essential info, fake parameters, queries naming a specific API, unreasonable broad queries (App A.7)

datasets.name: AnyToolBench
datasets.source: Built by authors with GPT-4 exploring the API pool, queries span 2 to 5 categories, reference solutions verified
datasets.preprocessing: Query at least thirty words; at most 20 initial meta-function calls (Table 21)

other.version: not stated for agents; judge is GPT-4-32K

inference.max_tokens: 200,000 tokens per query across all components
inference.prompting: Zero-shot bootstrap prompts per agent type (Tables 14-20); solver prompt adapted from ToolLLM with a give-up option and reason
inference.retrieval: Hierarchical agent search over category > tool > API; candidate pool max 32 or 64 (default not stated; Table 6), up to K=5 tools per tool agent (Table 7), solver max 10 API calls

parameters.self_reflection_rounds: avg 4.6; Fig 3 shows 4-6 rounds; max not stated

metrics.name: Pass rate (Eq 2)
metrics.definition: #Solved / (#Solved + #Unsolved), judged by GPT-4-32K on query and solution

baselines: ToolLLM (OpenAI TE / ToolLLM retriever + ToolLLaMA or GPT-4 DFSDT)
GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 with reference APIs, CoT and DFSDT
eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell, no seeds, no significance tests stated; GPT-4-32K judge with ToolBench prompt; human agreement 96.5% on G1-I; all baselines reproduced by authors.

prompts.text: You are APIGPT, with access to a database of APIs. This database is organized into the following categories: {categories}. Your task is to help users identify the relevant categories for their needs. ... Remember, your goal is not to answer the query directly but to identify all potentially relevant categories and assign them to agents. Once you have completed the assignment, call the 'Finish' function.

The current APIs have failed to solve the query, resulting in: {fail reason}. You need to analyze this result and seek additional APIs. It's possible that the tools lack the relevant APIs. In such cases, you should call the Finish function. Remember not to invent tool or API names.
The current APIs have failed to solve the query, and the reason is: {fail reason}. Please consider assigning more unexplored tools to the agents.
The current APIs have failed to solve the query, and the reason is: {fail reason}. Please consider assigning more unexplored categories to the agents.
